name: Gale Crater
blurb: Curiosity's landing area: Bradbury Landing on Aeolis Palus, Yellowknife Bay, and the plains crossed on the way to the foot of Mount Sharp.

projection.name: Equirectangular, Mars 2000 sphere (IAU), latTs 0, lon0 0
projection.note: x = R*lon, y = R*lat (radians). North-south distances are true; east-west distances are stretched by 1/cos(lat), so the game multiplies projected x offsets by cos(lat0).

grid.convention: sample (i,j) of a level is centred at x0+(i+0.5)*mpp, y0-(j+0.5)*mpp; tile (tx,ty) holds samples tx*tile.. and ty*tile..
grid.world: game X = east true metres from the site centre = (x - x_centre) * cos_lat0; game Z = south metres = y_centre - y; game Y = height_m - height.ref

height.encoding: height_m = offset + (R*256 + G) * scale; B = provenance
height.datum: Mars areoid (the mosaic is tied to the MOLA DEM)

provenance_byte.255: measured: MSL Gale merged DEM (HiRISE stereo where its pairs cover, which includes the traverse; CTX or HRSC stereo elsewhere; the product has no per-pixel source flag)
provenance_byte.65-254: blended: the feather between the 1 m posts and the 4 m overview of the same DEM (interpolated)
provenance_byte.64: in a fine level only: nothing finer here, use the coarser level (the base level never carries 64 at this site: there is no separate CTX DTM)

levelling.method: HiRISE low-pass (48 m box on a 16 m grid) replaced by the mosaic's own 4 m overview (same product, so a near no-op) low-pass; HiRISE high-pass kept as it is (gain 1)

imagery.colour: single-band (greyscale) sensors; any colour on screen is a tint applied by the game

levels.what: MSL Gale merged DEM (HiRISE stereo, with CTX and HRSC beyond it): its 4 m overview block-averaged to 16 m
MSL Gale merged DEM: the mosaic's own 4 m overview, as published
MSL Gale merged orthophoto mosaic: its 4 m overview cubic-resampled to 5 m
MSL Gale merged orthophoto mosaic (0.25 m, HiRISE) block-averaged to 2 m; pixels taken on the mosaic's own grid, under 8 cm off the site grid

gale_dem_4m.title: Mars MSL Gale Merged DEM 1m, version 3 (USGS Astrogeology): the mosaic's own 4 m overview, whole site
gale_dem_4m.composition: HiRISE stereo DEMs (12 pairs over the landing ellipse and the traverse) merged with CTX and HRSC DEMs beyond them, all tied to MOLA; the product carries no per-pixel source flag
gale_dem_4m.licence: Public domain (USGS / NASA / JPL-Caltech / University of Arizona), credit the authors; cite Calef III, F.J. and Parker, T., 2016, MSL Gale Merged Orthophoto Mosaic / MSL Gale Merged DEM, PDS Annex, U.S. Geological Survey

gale_ortho_4m.title: Mars MSL Gale Merged Orthophoto Mosaic 25cm, version 3 (USGS Astrogeology): the mosaic's own 4 m overview (a box average), whole site
gale_ortho_4m.composition: HiRISE orthophotos merged with CTX and HRSC images beyond them; greyscale stored as a palette index (index 0 no data, index i is grey i-1), used here as the index
gale_ortho_4m.licence: Public domain (USGS / NASA / JPL-Caltech / University of Arizona), credit the authors; cite Calef III, F.J. and Parker, T., 2016, MSL Gale Merged Orthophoto Mosaic, PDS Annex, U.S. Geological Survey

hirise_dtm.title: Mars MSL Gale Merged DEM 1m, version 3 (USGS Astrogeology): native 1 m posts, a band across the site
hirise_dtm.composition: HiRISE stereo DEMs where the 12 pairs cover (the landing ellipse and the traverse do), CTX and HRSC DEMs elsewhere on the same 1 m grid; no per-pixel source flag
hirise_dtm.licence: Public domain (USGS / NASA / JPL-Caltech / University of Arizona), credit the authors; cite Calef III and Parker 2016
hirise_dtm.bytes_measured_by: TIFF StripByteCounts of the 2816 rows read (247,774,709) plus the header reads (92,450)

hirise_ortho.title: Mars MSL Gale Merged Orthophoto Mosaic 25cm, version 3 (USGS Astrogeology): native 0.25 m pixels, a window from Yellowknife Bay to Cooperstown
hirise_ortho.composition: HiRISE orthophotos in this window; greyscale stored as a palette index (index 0 no data), used as the index
hirise_ortho.licence: Public domain (USGS / NASA / JPL-Caltech / University of Arizona), credit the authors; cite Calef III and Parker 2016
hirise_ortho.grid_shift_note: source pixels taken as they are; +x east, +y north: where the source grid sits relative to the site grid

pois.name: Bradbury Landing
pois.source: NASA/JPL MSL waypoints, site 2 drive 0 (sol 3 localisation of the landing site; the rover first drove on sol 16)

pois.name: Yellowknife Bay, John Klein
pois.note: Where Curiosity drilled its first rock, John Klein, on sol 182, and Cumberland on sol 279: mudstone laid down in an ancient lake.
pois.source: NASA/JPL MSL waypoints, site 6 drive 0 (end-of-drive localisation sol 166; the rover stayed within 2 m of it until sol 295)

pois.name: Darwin (Waypoint 1)
pois.note: The first science stop on the drive toward Mount Sharp: a conglomerate outcrop studied on sols 390 to 401.
pois.source: NASA/JPL MSL waypoints, site 16 drive 50 (end-of-drive localisation sol 392)

pois.name: Cooperstown (Waypoint 2)
pois.note: A layered outcrop examined with the arm on sols 440 to 453.
pois.source: NASA/JPL MSL waypoints, site 22 drive 0 (end-of-drive localisation sol 440)

notes: There is no separate CTX mosaic pair at this site: every level comes from the two USGS 'MSL Gale Merged' mosaics (DEM 1 m, orthophoto 0.25 m) or their own overviews.

Those mosaics merge HiRISE products with CTX and HRSC products where no HiRISE stereo pair exists, without a per-pixel source flag, so 'measured' here means 'in the published mosaic', and the true resolution away from the HiRISE pairs is coarser than the grid.

The orthophoto grid (origin 8126248, -241164; 0.25 m) is not aligned with the DEM grid: imagery windows take the nearest source pixels (no resampling), a shift of under 8 cm recorded in sources.hirise_ortho.grid_shift_m.
quality: MSL Gale merged mosaic (HiRISE, with CTX and HRSC beyond it): 5 m imagery and 4 m terrain everywhere; 2 m imagery and 4 m terrain along the traverse
